newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo LSWR trading lacklustre with high stocks.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo LSWR trading lacklustre with high stocks.

text.p: Tokyo low sulphur fuel oil trading was lacklustre on Monday as traders held on to high stocks, which were originally meant to be sold on to power firms during the summer peak season of electricity, fuel oil dealers said.
Fuel oil requirements from power firms usually jump in the summer as operations at thermal power plants get into full swing to cover increased electricity consumption.
However, this year's demand from the electric utilities has turned out to be smaller than expected as each heatwave has failed to last for more than a few days so far this year, traders said.
The naphtha market was largely quiet as most traders were still in a holiday mood, market participants said.
Many Japanese traders were away for the summer holidays last week.
"It is a real struggle to find out where the market levels are today," one naphtha trader said.
Offers for second-half October open-spec naphtha were heard at $205.50 per tonne, while bids were assessed at $204.50.
